cases.question: When does losing the ball while going to the ground make a pass incomplete?
answer_rubric: Losing control on ground contact before a football act (or sufficient time for one) makes the pass incomplete.
After all catch requirements are satisfied, maintaining control through the ground is not required; a later loss can be a fumble.
Contains no other material rule claim that contradicts or exceeds the supplied corpus evidence.

cases.question: He secures the pass, taps both toes inbounds, turns upfield, and only then loses the ball. Was the reception already completed?
answer_rubric: Concludes that the stated control, both toes inbounds, and turn upfield satisfy the catch requirements before the loss.
Explains that a later loss does not retroactively make that reception incomplete and may be a fumble.
Contains no other material rule claim that contradicts or exceeds the supplied corpus evidence.
